sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Only prosodic remark is fn. 9 (p. 206): 'ɕóː-ma belongs to a class of verbs that lost a final velar plosive in their transitive versions (perhaps compensated for by the high tone on the vowel)'; fn. 1 (p. 195) notes data are Kanam variety and vowel-quantity transcription may be inaccurate. Acute accent appears only on ɕóː-ma in the whole chapter.

sources.citation: Sharma, D. D. 1988. A Descriptive Grammar of Kinnauri (Studies in Tibeto-Himalayan Languages 1). Delhi: Mittal.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes STANDARD (Lower) Kinnauri [kinn1249], not Shumcho: sec. 5.5 pp. 45-46 'Kinnauri neither, like English, is a stressed language, nor, like Chinese, a tonal one.. Usually in a polysyllabic word the initial syllable has a higher stress and the non-initial a higher pitch.' Thebarskad (Kanam-Pooh area = Shumcho) is only listed as dialect group II on p. 6; no data from it.
